The check path validates only the approval target kind before rendering supplied approvals. It never binds their specification, claim-set, target, or reviewed digests to the current inputs, so stale or unrelated approvals can be incorporated into an expected document and accepted as conformant.

The check loader converts a signed approval to its binding and copies its key identifier without any signature or trust-key verification. Thus the signed form is treated as applied based only on parsed, attacker-controlled contents.

Manifest values are inserted without checking the prior entry, so repeating a key silently overwrites its earlier value. Invalid duplicate-key TOML is therefore accepted with last-value-wins behavior.

A table header uses entry(...).or_default(), so an already-defined table can be reopened and merged instead of being rejected. This accepts duplicate TOML table definitions and makes later entries alter the earlier section's scope.

The refine precondition checks for a mapping and the target layer's file, but not the refining layer's own file. The success branch then indexes section.values["file"], so a malformed refine layer without file panics instead of returning the structured error used for missing inputs.
